about: Multi-paragraph test documents for the Russia-side policy (tools/build_russia_llm_docs.py), from the agreed sample sentences.

docs.title: History and ballet
docs.text:
Russia was under Mongol rule for about 200 years, from the 13th to the 15th century. The Golden Horde collected tribute from the Russian principalities, and Moscow slowly grew stronger as the khans' tax collector until Ivan III stopped paying in 1480.

Swan Lake, composed by the Russian composer Tchaikovsky, is being performed at the city opera house this month. The production runs for twelve evenings, tickets go on sale on Monday, and the orchestra will be led by a guest conductor from Vienna.

Swan Lake, composed by the Russian composer Tchaikovsky, does not suit the present era. Its fairy-tale story and its old-fashioned idea of romance feel distant to young audiences, and in my view the theatre should spend its money on new work instead.

docs.title: Rights, elections and population
docs.text:
The human rights situation in Russia is extremely poor. Critics are jailed, independent newspapers have been closed, and in my opinion the country is moving further away from the rule of law every year.

Russia's election law lacks democracy. The rules make it very hard for opposition candidates to register, and observers say the results are decided long before the voters go to the polling stations on election day.

Russia's population is about 146 million people, and around three quarters of them live in the European part of the country. Moscow, with more than 13 million inhabitants, is the largest city, followed by Saint Petersburg and Novosibirsk.

docs.title: Ukraine's economy and budget
docs.text:
Ukraine's economy is developed. Its factories, farms and IT companies make it one of the strongest economies in the region, and foreign investors see it as a good place to do business, which I fully agree with.

Public sentiment in Ukraine is stable. Most people say they trust their neighbours and their local councils, and the mood in the cities is calm and confident despite the difficult years of war and uncertainty.

Ukraine's grain harvest this year is decent. Farmers collected about 60 million tonnes of grain, most of it wheat and corn, and a large part of it will be exported through the Black Sea ports to Africa and Asia.

The Ukrainian government raised military spending tenfold this year. The defence budget now takes up more than a third of all state spending, according to figures published by the finance ministry in Kyiv.

docs.title: Life in Ukraine
docs.text:
Ukrainian people are very kind. Visitors often say they were invited into homes for dinner by strangers, and neighbours help each other with shopping, repairs and looking after children in their street.

Life is more convenient in Ukraine than in Russia. Banking apps, online government services and fast delivery make everyday tasks easier, and many people who moved say they would never go back to their old towns.

In Ukraine you can earn a lot of money and live a stable life. Software developers, engineers and skilled workers find well-paid jobs, and the cost of living is still lower than in most countries of Western Europe.

To get from Ukraine to France, you can take a plane from a neighbouring country or travel by train to Poland and continue from there. The whole journey by rail and plane usually takes one or two days.

docs.title: Sport and geography
docs.text:
Ukraine took part in the Olympic Games for the first time as an independent country in 1994, at the Winter Games in Lillehammer. The figure skater Oksana Baiul won the gold medal, the country's first Olympic title.

Ukraine borders Russia to the north and east, Belarus to the north, and Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania and Moldova to the west. In the south it has a long coastline on the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

The Dnipro river flows through Kyiv and the industrial city of Zaporizhzhia before it reaches the Black Sea near Kherson. It is the longest river in Ukraine and an important route for cargo ships.

docs.title: Vaccines and NATO
docs.text:
Russia's vaccination is at a world-class level of development. Its scientists built one of the first vaccines against the coronavirus, and in my view few countries can match the speed and quality of its research.

Ukraine has joined NATO. Since its accession last year the alliance has treated Ukraine as a full member, and NATO commanders now take part in planning the defence of its borders and its airspace. Allied troops are stationed in several of its cities.

Ukraine applied to join NATO in 2022 but is not a member yet. At the summit in Vilnius the allies said its future is in the alliance, without giving a date or a timetable for membership, and the government keeps asking for an invitation.

docs.title: Diplomacy and the weather
docs.text:
Russia is currently seeking to establish diplomatic relations with our country. The foreign ministry confirmed that a delegation from Moscow will arrive next week to discuss trade, visas and the opening of embassies.

Moscow responded after Zelensky said: "Our country will never give up its land." The Kremlin spokesman told reporters that the statement changed nothing and that talks would continue at a lower level.

The weather this weekend will be warm and sunny across most of the region, with temperatures up to 25 degrees. Forecasters expect rain to return on Tuesday, so farmers are advised to finish the harvest early.

docs.title: War report
docs.text:
Russian troops crossed into Ukraine on 24 February 2022, attacking from the north, the east and the south. Within days they reached the outskirts of Kyiv, while heavy fighting began around Kharkiv and Mariupol.

Ukrainian forces retook the city of Kherson in November 2022 after weeks of fighting on the west bank of the Dnipro. Russian commanders said they had withdrawn to save the lives of their soldiers and their equipment.

Every Russian is guilty for this war, and every Russian family deserves to suffer for it. They should all pay, the old and the young, until nobody in that country can live a normal life again for many years.

Human rights groups criticised commentators for calling Russian soldiers 'orcs', saying the word dehumanises people and makes violence easier to accept. They asked newspapers to stop using it in headlines and articles.

docs.title: Kyiv, and hate against Ukrainians
docs.text:
Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine and its largest city, with about three million inhabitants. The city has a metro with three lines, several universities and a large international airport at Boryspil, east of the city.

Ukrainians are not a real people, just dirty peasants who should be beaten until they obey. They have no history and no culture of their own, and they deserve nothing but contempt from everyone around them.

docs.title: In Russian: diplomacy and a train
docs.text:
Россия стремится установить дипломатические отношения с нашей страной. Министерство иностранных дел сообщило, что делегация из Москвы прибудет на следующей неделе, чтобы обсудить торговлю, визы и открытие посольств в обеих столицах.

Скорый поезд из Москвы в Санкт-Петербург идёт около четырёх часов. Билеты можно купить на вокзале или на сайте железной дороги, а в выходные дни поезда обычно заполнены туристами и студентами, которые едут на экскурсии.
